title: The belief-action gap in language model agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.17444v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language model (LM) agents can fail for different reasons, requiring different explanations and interventions. We study how state beliefs, action values, and action preferences interact as LM agents reason and commit to decisions in text-rendered grid worlds. We estimate task-relevant beliefs using report-based and representation-based probes, and action values using inverse reinforcement learning. We find that task-relevant state and value information is often represented more reliably than it is reflected in behaviour. Tracking action preferences throughout reasoning further shows that decisions sharpen around a commitment point and reported belief uncertainty decreases near commitment, although individual belief changes do not consistently explain shifts in action preference. translated_title: 语言模型智能体中的信念-行动差距
translated_abstract: 语言模型（LM）智能体可能因不同原因而失败，因此需要不同的解释和干预措施。我们研究了在文本渲染的网格世界中，状态信念、动作价值和动作偏好在LM智能体进行推理并做出决策时是如何相互作用的。我们使用基于报告和基于表征的探测方法来估计与任务相关的信念，并使用逆强化学习来估计动作价值。我们发现，与任务相关的状态和价值信息在内部表征中往往比在行为中体现得更为可靠。在整个推理过程中追踪动作偏好进一步表明，决策会在某个“承诺点”附近逐渐明确，报告的信念不确定性也在接近承诺点时下降，尽管个体的信念变化并不能一致地解释动作偏好的转变。最后，当推理前缀从其他决策移植过来时，被强制执行的动作会遵循这些推理前缀，而所测试的推理窗口激活编辑仅提供有限的（干预效果）。
tldr: 研究发现语言模型智能体内部可靠地表征了任务相关的状态和价值信息，但这些信息并未可靠地体现在行为中，揭示了“信念-行动差距”，即智能体“知道”的内容与其“做出”的决策之间存在系统性不一致。
en_tdlr: This study reveals a belief-action gap in language model agents: task-relevant state and value information is often represented internally more reliably than it is reflected in behavior, meaning what agents "know" does not reliably translate into the decisions they make.
